# City of Malden

Malden City Hall · 215 Pleasant Street · Malden, MA 02148

# Meeting Minutes - Final · City Council

Council President Amanda Linehan · Councillor at Large Karen Colon Hayes · Councillor Paul Condon · Councillor Peg Crowe · Councillor at Large Michelle Luong · Councillor at Large Carey McDonald · Councillor Ryan O'Malley · Councillor Jadeane Sica · Councillor Chris Simonelli · Councillor Ari Taylor · Councillor Stephen Winslow

Tuesday, May 19, 2026 · 7:00 PM · City Council Chambers · 215 Pleasant Street · Malden, MA 02148 · Watch the meeting with Teams: https://tinyurl.com/46ppxcv6

## 1. CALL TO ORDER

Council President Linehan called the meeting to order at 7:22 PM. This evening's meeting began late secondary to the Finance Committee running behind scheduled while interviewing department heads on their projected FY'27 budgets.

## 2. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE & MOMENT OF SILENCE IN HONOR OF SERVICE MEMBERS

## 3. ROLL CALL

Also in attendance was Prasanna Rajasekaran and Lisa Cagno.

Present - Councillors: 9 - Paul Condon, Peg Crowe, Amanda Linehan, Carey McDonald, Ryan O'Malley, Chris

Simonelli, Ari Taylor, Stephen Winslow and Michelle Luong

Absent - Councillors: 2 - Karen Colon Hayes and Jadeane Sica

## 4. GUESTS, CITIZEN ACHIEVEMENT, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

Student representatives from Malden High School’s After School Development Program, in conjunction with Clean Water Action, will appear before the Council to present their project on water safety.

Youth Action Collaborative in conjunction with Clean Water Action gave an extensive presentation on PFAS in common household objects, climate change, disposal of hard to recycle products, and dangerous lead levels in local water supply. More information on this project may be found at https://cleanwater.org/ma-youth-action-collaborative.

## 5. PUBLIC COMMENT

There was nobody in attendance who signed up for Public Comment.

## 6. CONSENT AGENDA

### Approval of the Consent Agenda

A motion was made by Councillor Luong, seconded by Councillor Winslow to approve the Consent Agenda.The motion carried by unanimous vote.

**268-26** 

Minutes for the meeting of May 5, 2026

The Council Minutes were approved.

**269-26** 

Minutes for the meeting of May 12, 2026

Councillor Winslow asked to take Paper 269-26 off the consent agenda for the purpose of making an amendment to the meeting minutes from May 12 to include the following language:

Councillor Winslow noted that City Charter changes that went into effect in January 2026 removed the Traffic Commission from the Charter and the companion ordinances passed by the Council at the time it approved the Home Rule petition established a Transportation Commission to replace the role of the Traffic Commission. Ultimately, the Transportation Commission will be the body that enacts such a substantial change to our parking rules.

A motion was made by Councillor Winslow, seconded by Councillor Crowe, that the Council Minutes be amended. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

A motion was made by Councillor Winslow, seconded by Councillor Taylor, that the Council Minutes be approved as amended. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

## 7. MOTIONS, ORDERS, AND RESOLUTIONS

**275-26** 

Order: The Mayor will submit the Fiscal Year 2027 Annual Appropriation Orders for the Water Sewer Enterprise Fund, Community Preservation Fund, and Cable Access Fund.

Sponsors: Carey McDonald

Attachments: FY2027 Appropriation Orders for Water and Sewer, Cable Access, and Community Preservation

A motion was made by Councillor McDonald, seconded by Councillor Taylor, that the Order be referred to the Finance Committee. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

**276-26** 

Be it ordained by the Malden City Council that Sections 12 and 32 of Title 12 of the Code of the City of Malden (MCC) are hereby amended as outlined in the body of this paper regarding Data Centers:

Sponsors: Ari Taylor

Attachments: CCP 276-26 Planning Board Report June 10 2026

A motion was made by Councillor Taylor, seconded by Councillor O'Malley, that the Ordinance be referred to a joint session of the Planning Board with Rules & Ordinance. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

**277-26** 

The City Council will address the Open Meeting Law complaint submitted on May 13, 2026 by Bruce Friedman of 8 Marvin Street, Malden against the Council related to the Executive Session held on May 12, 2026.

Sponsors: Amanda Linehan

Attachments: Friedman OML 05.13.26 Response Final with exhibits

A motion was made by Councillor Simonelli, seconded by Councillor Luong, that the Council Item be referred to the Legal Department. The motion carried by an 8-0 vote. Councillor O'Malley voted present.

## 8. COMMITTEE REPORTS

A motion was made by Councillor Winslow, seconded by Councillor O'Malley, that the Committee Report be received and filed. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

Be it ordained by the Malden City Council that the Code of the City of Malden (MCC) 6.08.070 C(2) LICENSING OF MARIJUANA ESTABLISHMENTS is hereby amended by inserting ‘, provided that no fewer than five marijuana retailer licenses shall be made available.’ after ‘Mass. Gen. Laws ch 138 § 15’.

Yea: 9 - Condon, Crowe, Linehan, McDonald, O'Malley, Simonelli, Taylor, Winslow and Luong

## 9. TABLED PAPERS

**153-26** 

Petition: Massachusetts Electric Company dba National Grid Plan No. 31239416 -

National Grid to install underground facilities on Main Street. Trench and install (6) 4” concrete encased conduit from MH A/1 18 to switchgear located on 1100 Main Street approximately 60’ on public right of way. Malden, MA.

(Hearing Required)

Attachments: 1100 Main Street Petition

Abutters 1100 Main Street

Hearing Notice 1100 Main Street - Updated March 25, 2026

Updated Plan

1100 Main Street - landscaping plan

- 1100 Main Street - updated plan for electrical equipment w fencing
- buffers
- 1100 Main Street Petition Sketch May 19 2026

A motion was made by Councillor O'Malley, seconded by Councillor Winslow, that the Petition be taken from the table. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

Councillor O'Malley has been working quite some time in negotiations with National Grid and the property owner on this petition to make the equipment less of an eye sore to the surrounding community. The granting of the petition is contingent on the conditions that 1) The Engineer be called when Dig Safe is notified, 2) The streets and sidewalks be restored to the satisfaction of the Director of Public Works and 3) Per the landscaping plan, wooden cedar fencing buffer plan on the North and West side of the property, and electrical plans are followed subject to minor modifications and subject to final review of the Ward Councillor.

A motion was made by Councillor O'Malley, seconded by Councillor Winslow, that the Petition be granted with conditions. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

A motion was made by Councillor Simonelli, seconded by Councillor Luong, that this meeting be adjourned. The motion carried unanimously.
